topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture’s aims and connects its coverage of cancer genetics to the histopathology practicals.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how studies of transforming viruses established that cancer can arise through altered activity of normal cellular genes.

topics.label: Experimental assessment of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how experimental assays establish whether a gene or mutation gives cells transformed properties.

topics.label: Cancer gene classification and the functional effects of mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations are classified by their effects on tumor formation and why their specific molecular consequences determine how those classifications apply.

topics.label: Genetic instability and failures of genome maintenance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how failures to preserve genome fidelity generate genetic instability and its consequences for cancer cells.

topics.label: Mutation order and colorectal cancer progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how the timing of mutation acquisition, especially the early emergence of genetic instability, affects colorectal tumor progression.

topics.label: Inherited cancer predisposition and BRCA2 restoration
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inherited tumor-suppressor defects promote cancer development while the BRCA2 treatment example shows that the initiating defect need not remain necessary for malignancy.

topics.label: Closing, further reading, and questions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing concludes the lecture with an invitation for questions, recommended reading, and a preview of the next session.
